Grimace Shake
GRIM-us SHAYK
noun (Gen Alpha slang)
McDonald’s purple, berry-flavored milkshake, sold from June 12, 2023, for the birthday of Grimace, the round purple mascot introduced in 1971 (originally as the four-armed "Evil Grimace" who stole milkshakes). Within days a TikTok trend took over: a creator wishes Grimace a happy birthday, sips the shake, and the clip cuts to a staged horror scene — the person collapsed, "dead," or possessed, splattered with purple. Millions of copies followed, and "Grimace shake" became shorthand for a cursed object or a comic-horror twist.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

The Grimace shake was a purple McDonald’s milkshake, and the 2023 TikTok joke was that drinking it made you "die" — people filmed themselves taking a sip and then lying in a heap, covered in purple. Gen Alpha still calls something weird or dangerous a "Grimace shake." The Christian observation: the trend is comic horror, and much of it is just goofy. But it is goofy about death, and children absorbed a joke that death is a punchline and a prop. Scripture is not grim about death, but it is sober: "It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart" (Ecc 7:2). Moses prayed, "So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom" (Psa 90:12). The Christian can laugh at death only for one reason — because Christ has defeated it: "O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?" (1Co 15:55). Jesus came to "deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage" (Heb 2:15). A father can tell a five-year-old: "That was a pretend joke. Real dying is sad, but Jesus beat death, so people who love Him live forever with Him. That’s why we’re not afraid."

Webster 1828 Definition

McDonald’s purple birthday shake (June 2023) and the TikTok trend of staged "deaths" after a sip — comic horror that made death a prop, against Scripture’s sober and victorious view of the grave.

GRIMACE SHAKE, n. (McDonald’s, June 2023; TikTok trend) The purple birthday milkshake; the meme of a sip followed by a staged horror "death"; anything cursed. "Don’t drink that, it’s a Grimace shake."

Grimace: McDonald’s mascot since 1971 (first as "Evil Grimace").

Decode for parents: mostly silly; some younger children found the clips genuinely frightening.

Webster 1828, the root — SHAKE, v.t. To cause to move with quick vibrations; to move rapidly one way and the other; to agitate; as, the wind shakes a tree; an earthquake shakes the hills or the earth.

Key Scripture

Ecc 7:2 — "It is better to go to the house of mourning, than to go to the house of feasting: for that is the end of all men; and the living will lay it to his heart."

Psa 90:12 — "So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom."

1Co 15:55 — "O death, where is thy sting? O grave, where is thy victory?"

Heb 2:15 — "And deliver them who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage."

Modern Corruption

The Grimace-shake trend treated death as a slapstick prop; Scripture is sober about death and laughs at it only from the far side of the empty tomb.

expand to see more

Gallows humor is old, and the trend was mostly harmless theater. Its deeper effect is cultural: a generation that rarely sees real death sees thousands of comic fake ones. Death becomes unserious, a gag for views, and the sobriety Ecclesiastes commends — laying the end of all men to heart — grows harder.

Use the meme to talk about death plainly. Children are curious and often afraid. Tell them death is real and sad, that it came by sin, and that Jesus has defeated it. Then Christians can laugh at death the way Paul did — "where is thy sting?" — not because it is a joke, but because it has lost.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

English grimace (a twisted face; French) → McDonald’s mascot Grimace (1971) → Grimace Birthday shake (June 2023) → TikTok staged-death trend.
